planning_rules.rule: Move athlete from beginner loading options to intermediate progression options only after roughly 6 months of consistent resistance training plus stable technique.
recommended_action: keep progression one variable at a time
source_refs: ACSM Progression Models in Resistance Training
planning_rules.implementation_note: Use training history and completion consistency, not only self-reported level.

planning_rules.rule: Unlock advanced strength planning only when the athlete has multi-year training history, stable technique, and can tolerate consistent loading without readiness decline.
blocked_action: advanced methods during congested competition blocks
source_refs: ACSM Progression Models in Resistance Training
planning_rules.implementation_note: This is a conservative backend gate; no single universal strength number applies across all sports.

planning_rules.rule: Unlock low-level plyometrics when the athlete is pain-free or stable-low pain and can land, brace, and control basic positions.
planning_rules.implementation_note: Low-level plyos do not require the same strength gate as depth jumps.

planning_rules.rule: Reserve high-intensity reactive plyometrics for athletes with good mechanics, no pain, enough force capacity, and no current jump-load fatigue signal.
recommended_action: do early in session before fatigue
blocked_action: extra reactive plyos in high jump-count weeks
planning_rules.implementation_note: The often-cited 1.5x body-mass squat standard is best stored as a high-intensity depth-jump heuristic, not a universal plyometric rule.

planning_rules.rule: Unlock sprinting and max-velocity exposure only after easy running or submaximal running is tolerated with normal mechanics and stable 24-hour response.
recommended_action: separate from heavy eccentric lower-body work
blocked_action: max velocity after 4+ week layoff without reconditioning
sprinting when symptoms worsen next day
source_refs: Ohio State Basic Return to Running Guideline
planning_rules.implementation_note: Use symptom and gait gates because no universal max-speed numeric prerequisite exists.

planning_rules.rule: Unlock low-complexity Olympic-lift derivatives before full clean/snatch variations.
blocked_action: heavy catch variations with poor mobility
planning_rules.implementation_note: Full lifts require a higher technical gate than pulling derivatives.

planning_rules.rule: Advanced strength methods should only be used when simpler progressive overload is no longer sufficient and the athlete has enough recovery space.
blocked_action: advanced methods when completion is poor
source_refs: ACSM Progression Models in Resistance Training
planning_rules.implementation_note: Use as a planner upgrade, not a default method.

planning_rules.rule: Do not progress. Reduce load, impact, range, or complexity until symptoms return to baseline.
recommended_action: flag for clinical review if severe or persistent
source_refs: Ohio State Basic Return to Running Guideline
planning_rules.implementation_note: This should override normal progression rules.

planning_rules.rule: Avoid adding new high-speed, high-impact, or high-skill/high-load stressors on low-sleep days.
recommended_action: keep strength at maintenance intensity if needed
planning_rules.implementation_note: Sleep threshold is an operational safety rule; combine with readiness and RPE when available.

planning_rules.rule: Hold progression and repeat, reduce, or simplify the current tier when effort is excessive or completion is poor.
recommended_action: prioritize consistency before unlocking riskier work
source_refs: ACSM Progression Models in Resistance Training
planning_rules.implementation_note: Completion gate is an SFTC operational heuristic, not a universal published cutoff.

planning_rules.rule: Downshift one or more training tiers after a meaningful layoff and rebuild exposure gradually before resuming prior speed, plyometric, or high-load work.
recommended_action: reduce volume by 30-50% from previous peak
progress impact every other day when returning to running
source_refs: Ohio State Basic Return to Running Guideline
planning_rules.implementation_note: For strength sports, exact layoff thresholds are less standardized; use conservative tier downshift.

planning_rules.rule: Insert a load-reduction or maintenance microcycle when monotony is high and readiness is worsening.
planning_rules.implementation_note: Use only when SFTC has reliable sRPE/load tracking.

sport_profiles.planning_summary: Role-specific sport with especially strict workload protection for fast bowlers. Bowling exposure, throwing load, fielding speed, trunk capacity, and shoulder health must be tracked separately.
source_refs: Cricket Australia Junior Pace Bowling Guidelines
ASCA professional cricket skill-conditioning case study

sport_profiles.planning_summary: Jump load, landing exposure, overhead volume, and tendon health drive planning. In-season strength should maintain output while limiting soreness and unnecessary extra contacts.
source_refs: USA Volleyball Strength and Conditioning in Volleyball

sport_profiles.planning_summary: Use a match-centered microcycle. Heavier field and gym work belongs farther from match day; MD-2 and MD-1 should reduce fatigue. Starters and low-minute players need different post-match logic.
source_refs: Silva et al. soccer strength review
Ammann et al. professional soccer microcycle study

sport_profiles.planning_summary: Aerobic-dominant planning with careful quality placement, conservative run-volume progression, consistent strength support, and tapering by volume reduction before priority races.
source_refs: Haugen et al. world-class distance running review
Strength training in distance runners review

sport_profiles.planning_summary: Long season, travel, game congestion, jump exposure, ankle risk, and patellar tendon load shape planning. In-season lifting is usually one to two short total-body sessions.
source_refs: Human Kinetics in-season basketball training excerpt
Chronic ankle instability in basketball study

sport_profiles.planning_summary: Technical training stays central, while strength, conditioning, sparring, tapering, and weight management must be sequenced to avoid camp fatigue and unsafe dehydration-driven planning.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Only progress if completion is stable and pain returns to baseline within 24h.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Week 4 reduce volume 20-30% if readiness declines; otherwise hold load.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Increase volume first, then intensity. Add low-level plyometrics only if movement gate passes.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Every 4th week reduce volume or complexity.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Progress impact and speed separately; do not increase both in same week.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Use readiness-based deload.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Move to intermediate only if training history, completion, pain, and movement gates pass.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Week 24 testing or low-volume consolidation.

phase_sequence.gym_frequency: 3-4/week off-season; 2-3/week if sport practice is high
phase_sequence.progression_logic: Build volume gradually before pushing load.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Deload week 4 or 8 based on readiness.

phase_sequence.sport_frequency: moderate; keep high-intensity sport work controlled
phase_sequence.progression_logic: Increase intensity while trimming junk volume.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Deload every 4th week or after high RPE trend.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Add power only after strength and technique gates pass.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Reduce volume, keep quality.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Test submaximal or technical benchmarks; avoid max testing if readiness poor.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Low volume testing week.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Keep reps low and intent high; avoid fatigue circuits.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Week 4 reduce contacts and accessory volume.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Progress intensity or complexity, not total fatigue.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Reduce volume if jump/speed quality drops.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Maintain output and reduce residual fatigue.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Taper in final 7-14 days before priority event if applicable.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Start with submaximal exposures and controlled deceleration.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Reduce sprint volume if soreness or mechanics worsen.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Increase intensity before volume; separate max-speed from heavy eccentric work.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Every 4th week or readiness-triggered.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Use low-volume high-quality exposure; stop when quality drops.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Reduce volume, maintain speed touches.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Move to competition-week logic if match exists.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Taper volume in final week.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: No aggressive overload; establish maintenance dose.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Reduce gym volume after high match minutes.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Use match calendar first, gym second.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Auto-deload during congested weeks.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Maintain intensity touch, reduce volume.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Use competition-week rules before key matches.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Progress only if 24-hour response is stable.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: No deload; stay conservative.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Increase only one variable per week: volume, intensity, impact, or complexity.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Hold or regress immediately if pain response fails.

phase_sequence.progression_logic: Unlock normal template only after completion, pain, and readiness gates pass.
phase_sequence.deload_logic: Week 8 assessment and consolidation.

competition_week_rules.rule: Avoid high-volume lower-body strength, exhaustive conditioning, high-impact plyometric load, and novel exercises.

source_refs: Ammann et al. professional soccer microcycle
Cricket Australia Junior Pace Bowling Guidelines

competition_week_rules.rule: Reduce total volume substantially while maintaining intensity and most training frequency.
competition_week_rules.volume_guidance: Approximate 41-60% volume reduction for key taper when appropriate.
